figures.core_claim: The full local Fisher spectrum can spend a finite codebook too narrowly, while SCF restores directional coverage and improves held-out attention behavior at the same representation rate.

panels.a: Equal-rate schematic with two explicit 12-codeword grids; conceptual rather than empirical.
panels.b: Cumulative normalized metric spectrum for the full Fisher spectrum with a 50% identity floor and SCF across 256 layer-head matrices.
panels.c: Paired held-out attention KL across eight frozen windows.
panels.d: Aggregate relative changes in error under M_F, logit MSE, attention KL, and raw error.

reviewer_risks: The diagnostic is one model/backend setting and must not be presented as universal proof.
The raw-MSE trade-off must remain visible so the plot does not imply improvement in every metric.
Panel c has eight deterministic windows, not independent training seeds.
figures.self_review_revision: Placed all four panels in equal-width columns, expanded the schematic downward, moved panel labels upward, tightened export and caption spacing, replaced both curve-overlapping labels in panel b with compact lower-right keys whose colored line samples are explicitly equal in length, removed the ambiguous mean diamonds from panel c, and verified the result at final double-column size.

figures.core_claim: Relative to Euclidean assignment, SCF provides the larger PPL reduction at lower rates, while the full-spectrum Fisher control with the same identity floor and SCF converge at 2 BPA.

panels.a: WikiText-2 PPL reduction relative to the rate-matched Euclidean parent.
panels.b: C4 PPL reduction relative to the rate-matched Euclidean parent.

reviewer_risks: The panels show point estimates; significance is described in the manuscript rather than encoded as error bars.
Both panels must retain one shared y-axis to avoid visually exaggerating dataset differences.
Relative reduction must be interpreted against the rate-matched Euclidean parent, not across datasets.
figures.self_review_revision: Replaced the dense attribution table with two aligned rate-trend panels, used a shared zero-based scale, made SCF visually dominant, retained marker and line-style redundancy for grayscale reading, and added an explicit higher-is-better axis cue.

figures.core_claim: The fixed p=0.5, alpha=0.5 SCF geometry lies in a useful local power/floor neighborhood on the frozen LLaMA-3-8B/GSRQ/C4/0.75-BPA setting.
reviewer_risks: This is a post-hoc one-setting robustness study and cannot select a new default.
All five new cells and both reused comparators must retain their sealed provenance.
Mixed or negative outcomes must remain visible.
figures.self_review_revision: Rejected the first render because the long vertical label clipped at single-column size; shortened the label, moved panel letters inward, placed the SCF labels below the default diamonds to separate them from the fixed-parameter titles, then accepted the final render after checking all four exports.

figures.core_claim: Full-spectrum Fisher selector concentration and SCF broadening, both under the same identity floor, recur under the same GSRQ protocol on a second language-model backbone.

panels.a: Cumulative final selector-metric spectrum across 256 Meta-Llama-3-8B layer-head matrices.
panels.b: The same spectrum statistic across 256 Mistral-7B-v0.1 layer-head matrices.

reviewer_risks: The Mistral panel replicates only the spectral trend, not the held-out attention-KL diagnostic.
The two source artifacts must retain the same 32-layer, 8-head, 128-D, 8-window, 512-sample protocol.
The curves aggregate layer-head matrices; the interquartile band is not a confidence interval over model seeds.
figures.self_review_revision: Used a single-column two-panel layout with shared axes and legend, retained line-style redundancy for grayscale, added the leading-13 guide, renamed the full-spectrum control to make the shared identity floor explicit, and accepted the final render after inspecting the raster at manuscript size.
